diagnosis.root_cause: The router has never reported a heartbeat, so its management-plane reachability or heartbeat monitoring is not established. This is not a subscriber access outage: the ONU is online, optics are stable, authentication is consistent, the expected VLAN is present, and traffic is passing.
evidence: The scheduled scan targets the router, and its heartbeat status is never with no check-in record.
The ONU is currently online and responds to SNMP with RX power -21.9 dBm and TX power 2.34 dBm, both within normal EPON ranges.
Seven days of RX, TX, distance, bias current, voltage, and temperature telemetry are stable; there is no fibre degradation, laser degradation, or distance change.
All visible peers on EPON0/4 are online, so there is no ONU, splitter, or PON-port outage.
The OLT answers ping and SNMP, has normal CPU, memory, temperature, and all six tested PONs are healthy; this is not an OLT fault.
Authentication is normal with an existing consistent RADIUS entry, three sessions in 24 hours, and session duration near the network mean.
The expected customer VLAN 1124 is present and correct.
Traffic is active and stable, confirming that customer service is currently passing despite the missing router heartbeat.

remediation.action: Verify the router's management connectivity, heartbeat agent, monitoring configuration, and firewall/ACL rules. Establish a heartbeat record and re-run the router probe. Do not replace the ONU, PON port, OLT, RADIUS configuration, or VLAN based on this case.

ground_truth.root_cause: The router has no check-in record of any kind, which means it was never enrolled in heartbeat monitoring rather than that it stopped responding. Its customers are authenticated, holding long sessions and passing normal traffic.
expected_reasoning: The router's heartbeat status is 'never' with a null last_checkin
That is different from a heartbeat that went stale, which would carry a timestamp and an elapsed time
No record at all indicates the router was never enrolled in the check-in mechanism
The ONU behind it is online with RX -21.9 and TX 2.3, both normal
The live probe confirms the ONU and its peers are all responding normally
Sessions are active with a 683 minute mean, close to the 11.9 hour network norm
Daily traffic is steady across all seven days with no interruption
Customers on this router are being served, so there is no outage
The finding is a monitoring gap, not a network fault

expected_escalation.review_reason: Router is not enrolled in heartbeat monitoring and should be added

distractors: A null heartbeat looks worse than a stale one and invites a Disaster conclusion
A scheduled scan targeting the router frames it as the suspect
The correct answer is that nothing is wrong with the network
